pr_title: Retrieve the `stack_index` from `Node` in `extract_ui_material_nodes` instead of walking `UiStack`
pr_body:
# Objective

 `ExtractedUiMaterialNode` is still walking the whole `UiStack`. 

more info: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/9853

fixes #9875

## Solution

Retrieve the `stack_index` from the `Node` component instead.
Also changed the `stack_index` field of `ExtractedUiMaterialNode` to `u32`.

issue_context.title: Remove `ZIndex::Global`
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

* It doesn't seem very useful, particularly since #9637 was merged.

* Almost no one seems to use it. I can't think of anything it allows you to do, that you can't do without it. CSS only has a local ZIndex.

* It's quite expensive for something no one uses. `ui_stack_system` constructs a new tree of `StackingContext`s each update. Without `ZIndex::Global`, we could update the UI stack in a single walk of the layout tree.

## What solution would you like?

Remove it.
comments:
I agree that global z-index is not strictly necessary. There are other ways to achieve most of what it brings to the table at the moment by using multiple roots, so it's not a necessary feature, especially if it comes a measurable performance hit even when unused.

It's not true that Web (CSS) only has local zindex though. That would imply that a child can't render on top of its parent, which is possible. Instead, it has a pretty complex system of [stacking contexts](https://web.dev/learn/css/z-index/) with rules that are notoriously hard to reason about. When I worked on this feature I didn't want to replicate that complexity, but I still added global z-index because I figured it could be useful as a simplified system. 

Whether this really is a desired feature is debatable though. On simple UIs it's generally not needed, but on the Web, this is often used for rendering deeply nested dropdowns and modals on top of everything else without having to add them to the root (body), and keeping the hierarchy which has effects other than just positioning and ordering (e.g. style inheritence, selectors, etc)

Ah ok, my naive understanding of CSS was that ZIndex was local and created new stacking contexts to rearrange items that shared the same parent, unless there was some other property that created a new stacking context such as `transform`.

> Whether this really is a desired feature is debatable though. On simple UIs it's generally not needed, but on the Web, this is often used for rendering deeply nested dropdowns and modals on top of everything else without having to add them to the root (body), and keeping the hierarchy which has effects other than just positioning and ordering (e.g. style inheritence, selectors, etc)

I strongly prefer the simplicity of ordering elements only by their position in the layout tree. Perhaps with the right API there might be a better way to do propagation of properties and events etc across the hierarchy without `ZIndex::Global`, I'm not sure.

Okay changed my mind on this but not exactly:
* `ZIndex::Global` should definitely be removed, `ZIndex` shouldn't be an enum. 
* We replace it with a separate `GlobalZIndex` component. This allows us to fix all the remaining performance issues with more precise query filters.
@ickshonpe Wanted to mention that `ZIndex` is the only ui component that doesn't implement `PartialEq`. This came up because I was writing unit tests for styling which needed to compare results.

review_comments: Not directly related to this PR, but is there a reason we are not using `parent_width` instead of `uinode.size().x` in these calculations?

Definitely a bug. The extraction system is meant to retrieve the size of the node's parent in a separate query (or use the width of the viewport if it is a root node). Instead here it's basing percentage border values on the node's own width, which is incorrect.
